newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shippers seek delay in air cargo surcharge.
newsitem.headline: French shippers seek delay in air cargo surcharge.

text.p: The French shippers council, Association des Utilisateurs de Transport de Fret (AUTF) said it is seeking the postponement of air freight surcharges announced by airlines in the past fortnight.

"The surcharges amount to unilateral action by several major airlines and were applied without prior notice or consultation with either shippers or air freight forwarding agents," AUTF's director of international transport, Herve Cornede, told Reuters.
"We find it totally incomprehensible and unacceptable ..and AUTF wholeheartedly condemned the surcharges," he said.
"We are calling for their postponement pending a genuine dialogue between the different parties involved," Cornede added.
The AUTF position is similar to the stand taken earlier this week by the French air freight forwarding association, SNAGFA.
Airlines which have announced freight surcharges, or in some cases a rate increase, include Air France, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, British Airways Plc,Swissair and Cargolux.
The average increase is US10 cents a kg although some routes may have different rates.
Industry sources added some carriers, which have not formally taken a decision to increase rates themselves, have however followed a national carrier's decision for business in the latter's country.
Thus Thai Airways International Ltd has followed British Airways introducing a cargo fuel surcharge ex-London, they said.

"We have confirmation from some airlines that they won't be applying surcharges while other are hesitating However, clearly Europe's principal airfreight carriers are applying such charges," Cornede added.
The airlines' unilateral step went against the way business is done today and shippers and forwarding agents would not bow to the "take or leave it" approach adopted, Cornede added.

"Our members are operating in a difficult economic climate too with rising raw materials and energy costs but you won't find them upping their prices. Fiercely competitive international markets do not allow increases to be systematically passed onto customers. Why should airlines be a category apart?" he asked.
